# Names reserved by generated code are rejected or escaped
<!-- GENERATED from the Phrase Board (issue #203, sha256:789e70634907700d7f46ec90f5f47fe86eae2e601f22fba65a35f3e37e78fbb7). Do not edit this file: edit the issue. -->


- **Status:** Ready
- **Shape:** Story
- **Type:** compiler (S)
- **Milestone:** Purpose: verifiability, preserved intent and reviewability
- **Source:** Review of card 193 (2026-10-29): generated code defines AvowryRuntime, AvowryFailure, AvowAttribute and a class Avows; an avow, type or module with a colliding name produces a C# compile error (for example CS0542) instead of a language diagnostic. The same exposure existed under the old names.
- **Depends on:** none
- **Story:** As Dana, I want a clear language diagnostic when a name I chose collides with a name the generated code needs, so that I do not meet an unexplained C# error.
- **Acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then; at most 3, each failing on partial work):**
  1. Given a module, type or avow whose generated name equals one the generated code reserves (AvowryRuntime, AvowryFailure, AvowAttribute, Avows, AvowSpecs, AvowryBuild or a method named like its containing generated class), When it is built, Then the build fails with a diagnostic naming the reserved name and the line, before any C# is generated
  2. Given a corpus fixture per reserved name family, When the iterating test runs, Then each pins the new diagnostic code and line, and valid near-misses still build
  3. Given the gate and CI, When the card is merged, Then both are green and generated C# of valid sources is unchanged

## Context

- Decide first whether to reject (a diagnostic) or to escape the colliding name; reject is the default because it keeps the generated code unchanged. The new code is listed in GRAMMAR.md at the next re-freeze. Follow docs/CODING_GUIDELINES.md.
